meta.disclaimer: Indicative FinOps maturity screen based on self-reported inputs and consultant diagnostic probes. Scores reflect the responses given and are intended to prioritize advisory action, not to certify compliance or commit to savings. Not a financial audit. Adapted in part from the FinOps Framework by the FinOps Foundation (CC BY 4.0), with changes by LTM; not endorsed by the FinOps Foundation.
meta.gating_note: Maturity is the highest stage passed with all preceding stages also passed. A stage passes only when its weighted score meets the threshold AND every critical checkpoint question meets the critical minimum threshold.

sources.name: FinOps Framework, FinOps Foundation (CC BY 4.0), adapted
FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification (FOCUS 1.0)
State of FinOps 2026 (FinOps Foundation practitioner survey)

stages.name: Chaos / Crawl Baseline
stages.desc: Foundational governance, security root boundaries, and raw billing data ingestion must exist before meaningful FinOps work can begin.
stages.aim: Establish who owns what, eliminate rogue unallocated spend, and ingest trustworthy raw billing data.
stages.leap_guide: To graduate from Chaos to Informed: (1) Formalize an account registry with a single named owner per subscription; (2) Ingest raw cloud billing exports into central S3/Blob storage; (3) Mandate the 3 core tags (CostCenter, Owner, App) on all compute resources.

stages.name: Informed / Walk Foundation
stages.desc: Cost visibility, tagging discipline (≥80%), scheduled showback cadence, and anomaly detection are established across business units.
stages.aim: Make spend visible and attributable, detect unexpected cost anomalies within 24h, and build regular monthly review cadences.
stages.leap_guide: To graduate from Informed to Optimized: (1) Shift from mere reporting to active waste elimination; (2) Establish a centralized commitment discount strategy (RIs/Savings Plans coverage ≥ 70%); (3) Allocate shared container and Kubernetes clusters by namespace.

stages.name: Optimized / Rate & Usage
stages.desc: The enterprise actively reduces waste, optimizes commitment-based rates, rightsizes compute/storage, and evaluates cost in architecture reviews.
stages.aim: Convert visibility into recurring, measurable savings and embed cost consciousness into engineering sprints.
stages.leap_guide: To graduate from Optimized to Automated: (1) Replace manual Jira tickets with automated policy-as-code guardrails; (2) Implement automated non-prod parking schedules; (3) Put FinOps efficiency metrics into engineering OKRs and performance reviews.

stages.name: Automated / Run Practice
stages.desc: Cost governance is enforced programmatically through policy-as-code pipelines, auto-parking, storage tiering, and engineering KPIs.
stages.aim: Make the efficient path the default path without manual friction, and extend FinOps to modern GenAI/GPU workloads.
stages.leap_guide: To graduate from Automated to Transparent: (1) Transition from showback to automated multi-tenant chargeback; (2) Model real-time unit economics (cost per transaction/tenant/API); (3) Integrate cloud unit costs directly into product pricing and gross margin models.

stages.name: Transparent / Unit Economics
stages.desc: Full financial accountability, real-time unit economics, margin forecasting, and direct integration into product roadmaps and pricing.
stages.aim: Run cloud as a core business driver, priced, margin-managed, and optimized for maximum shareholder value.
stages.leap_guide: At Stage 5 (Transparent): Focus on continuous posture defensibility, real-time margin defense, automated vendor contract renegotiations, and carbon sustainability unit economics.

checkpoints.title: Account Ownership & Scoped Access Model
checkpoints.desc: Named technical & business owners assigned per account/subscription with least-privilege billing console access.

checkpoints.title: Centralized Raw Billing Ingestion
checkpoints.desc: Granular hourly/daily cost & usage data exported to centralized, durable storage (S3/GCS/Blob).

checkpoints.title: Basic Billing Alarms & Spend Thresholds
checkpoints.desc: Active budget threshold alerts configured to fire before bills unexpectedly surge.

checkpoints.title: Finance Direct Cost Console Visibility
checkpoints.desc: Finance & procurement have self-service read-only access to billing data without ticketing engineering.

checkpoints.title: Production & Non-Prod Account Isolation
checkpoints.desc: Separate accounts/subscriptions with clear billing boundaries between production and sandbox/dev estates.

checkpoints.title: Comprehensive Tagging Policy (≥80% coverage)
checkpoints.desc: Documented tagging strategy with CostCenter, Owner, and App tags actively enforced on ≥80% compute/storage.

checkpoints.title: Multi-Cloud Normalization & FOCUS Readiness
checkpoints.desc: Billing data mapped to standardized taxonomy or FOCUS 1.0 format across hyperscalers.

checkpoints.title: Scheduled Showback Reporting Cadence
checkpoints.desc: Bi-weekly or monthly showback reports distributed directly to engineering team leads and BUs.

checkpoints.title: Automated Anomaly Detection
checkpoints.desc: Algorithmic cost anomaly detection alerting on unexpected spend spikes within 24 hours.

checkpoints.title: Month-over-Month Variance Accountability
checkpoints.desc: Engineering and product leads can explain month-over-month cloud cost variances with business drivers.

checkpoints.title: Commitment Discount Coverage (≥70%)
checkpoints.desc: ≥70% of steady-state compute covered by RIs, Savings Plans, or CUDs with centralized portfolio management.

checkpoints.title: Continuous Rightsizing Review & Execution
checkpoints.desc: Bi-weekly/monthly cadence where rightsizing and idle resource recommendations are actively deployed.

checkpoints.title: Container & Kubernetes Cost Allocation
checkpoints.desc: Shared cluster costs broken down by namespace, pod, service, or tenant (e.g. Kubecost, OpenCost).

checkpoints.title: Spot & Transient Compute Workload Adoption
checkpoints.desc: Eligible stateless, batch, or non-critical workloads leverage Spot/Preemptible instances with automated eviction handling.

checkpoints.title: Policy-as-Code Guardrails & Enforcement
checkpoints.desc: Automated enforcement (OPA, Terraform Sentinel, Azure Policy, SCPs) blocking non-compliant or untagged provisioning.

checkpoints.title: Automated Non-Prod Environment Parking
checkpoints.desc: Development and test environments automatically parked outside of core business hours.

checkpoints.title: Storage Lifecycle & Snapshot Auto-Pruning
checkpoints.desc: Automated lifecycle policies tiering object storage and purging unattached snapshots/disks by TTL.

checkpoints.title: AI / GenAI & GPU Spend Governance
checkpoints.desc: GPU cluster utilization tracking, idle model endpoint shutoff, and token inference cost attribution.

checkpoints.title: Automated Multi-Tenant Chargeback
checkpoints.desc: Direct financial cross-charging to business unit P&Ls with auditable allocation of shared platforms.

checkpoints.title: Real-Time Unit Economics Tracking
checkpoints.desc: Cloud spend measured against business metrics (cost per transaction, cost per active user, cost per API call).

checkpoints.title: Product Pricing & Gross Margin Integration
checkpoints.desc: Cloud unit costs feed directly into product pricing, enterprise client contract margins, and CFO forecasting.

checkpoints.title: Near-Zero Waste Posture (<4% bill)
checkpoints.desc: Orphaned, idle, and unallocated cloud waste consistently held under 4% of total estate spend.

questions.text: Is there an account-ownership and access model that supports cost governance (named owners per account, least-privilege access to billing and cost consoles)?

options.label: Yes — named owners on every account, scoped billing access documented
Ownership mostly assigned, access permissions ad hoc
Owners named for some accounts only
Neither owners nor access model defined

questions.consultant_probe: Ask to inspect their cloud organizational hierarchy (AWS Organizations / Azure Management Groups / GCP Resource Manager). Verify whether individual subscriptions have documented business & technical owners or are orphaned under former employees.
questions.subjective_prompt: Document client's account ownership structure, billing console access policies, and any known orphaned subscriptions.
questions.remediation: Establish named owners for every account/subscription and a documented access model for billing and cost consoles — the foundation FinOps decisions attach to.

questions.text: Is granular billing and usage data exported to a centralised, durable store (e.g. CUR to S3, Cost Management export to Azure Blob, Cloud Billing export to BigQuery)?

options.label: Yes — daily/hourly granular export active to a central bucket for all cloud accounts
Export enabled for primary cloud accounts only
Billing data viewed in console only; no automated export
No centralised access to billing data

questions.consultant_probe: Verify if raw hourly/daily Cost & Usage Reports (CUR / FOCUS-ready exports) are enabled and flowing to an immutable analytical bucket, or if teams rely solely on 30-day portal summaries.
questions.subjective_prompt: Note data export frequency, storage destination, retention policy, and whether multiple cloud providers are consolidated.
questions.remediation: Enable automated daily/hourly billing exports (AWS CUR 2.0, Azure Cost Export, GCP BigQuery Export) to an analytical data lake — without granular data, attribution and optimization are impossible.

questions.text: Are billing alarms or spend threshold notifications configured and actively alerting when spend crosses defined thresholds?

options.label: Yes — proactive threshold alerts on all accounts, routed to active communication channels (Slack/Teams/Email)
Alarms configured for some accounts or at high threshold only
Configured historically but alerts are ignored or misrouted
No billing alarms or spend alerts exist

questions.consultant_probe: Ask when the last unexpected spend surge occurred. Were they alerted by an automated notification, or did they only find out when the monthly invoice arrived?
questions.subjective_prompt: Document current alert configuration, distribution lists, and false-positive / alert-fatigue issues.
questions.remediation: Configure automated spend alerts at 50%, 80%, and 100% of budgeted spend with routing to active engineering communication channels.

questions.text: Does the finance team have direct read-only access to cloud billing consoles and cost dashboards without needing engineering tickets?

options.label: Yes — finance has self-service, read-only access to cloud billing tools and portals
Finance receives periodic manual reports from engineering on request
Finance sees the top-level invoice only with no line-item visibility
Finance has no direct visibility into cloud spend

questions.consultant_probe: Ask Finance how they reconcile month-end invoices. Do they wait 2 weeks for an engineering manager to manually pull a CSV, or can they self-service in the cloud console?
questions.subjective_prompt: Capture current finance workflow, invoice reconciliation delay, and any friction between finance and cloud architects.
questions.remediation: Grant Finance and procurement read-only billing IAM roles (e.g. AWS BillingReadOnlyAccess, Azure Cost Management Reader) to eliminate invoice blind spots.

questions.text: Does an account / subscription ownership registry exist with a named technical and business owner per account?

options.label: Yes — comprehensive registry maintained and reviewed on account provisioning
Registry exists but is partially out of date or missing some business owners
Informal knowledge of who owns which accounts
No account registry exists

questions.consultant_probe: Ask for the registry document or CMDB extract. Check if ownership is maintained in an automated service catalog or an outdated spreadsheet from two years ago.
questions.subjective_prompt: Assess accuracy of the account registry and how new cloud accounts are provisioned and registered.
questions.remediation: Mandate an Account Ownership Registry integrated into your Identity Provider (Okta/Entra ID) and account vending pipeline.

questions.text: Are production and non-production environments strictly separated into distinct cloud accounts/subscriptions with clear billing boundaries?

options.label: Yes — strict separation into separate accounts/subscriptions with isolated billing
Separated by VPC / Resource Group but sharing the same account / subscription
Partially mixed environments across legacy workloads
Production and non-production share the same accounts with no boundary

questions.consultant_probe: Inspect whether developers have permissions to spin up GPU or high-memory instances in the same AWS account / Azure subscription that hosts production workloads.
questions.subjective_prompt: Note environment segmentation architecture, sandbox policies, and cost containment guardrails.
questions.remediation: Isolate production, staging, and sandbox environments into dedicated accounts/subscriptions to prevent non-prod experiments from polluting production billing.

questions.text: Is a single team or individual formally accountable for cloud spend governance (e.g. CCoE, FinOps Champion, Cloud Architect)?

options.label: Yes — formally chartered FinOps team or lead with documented responsibilities
Informally owned by a cloud lead alongside other infrastructure duties
FinOps responsibilities fragmented across engineering leads with no coordination
No team or individual is accountable for cloud spend governance

questions.consultant_probe: Ask who owns the cloud budget variance conversation. If everyone says 'everyone is responsible', in practice nobody is accountable.
questions.subjective_prompt: Document existing FinOps/CCoE charter, reporting line (CFO vs CTO), and time dedication.
questions.remediation: Appoint a dedicated FinOps Lead or formalize a Cloud Center of Excellence (CCoE) cross-functional charter with Finance and Engineering representation.

questions.text: Are root credentials, multi-cloud master payer accounts, and enterprise agreement portals properly secured with MFA and restricted billing console roles?

options.label: Yes — master payer isolated, root MFA enforced, dedicated billing IAM roles
Master payer secured, but billing role access is loosely restricted
Shared administrator logins used for billing consoles
No access controls or MFA on root/master billing consoles

questions.consultant_probe: Check how master payer accounts (AWS Management Account / Azure Enterprise Agreement portal) are accessed and who can purchase savings plans or marketplace items.
questions.subjective_prompt: Document master payer security, marketplace commitment approval gates, and IAM controls.
questions.remediation: Lock down root billing credentials with hardware MFA and enforce least-privilege IAM roles for purchasing and marketplace commitments.

questions.text: Is a tagging / metadata strategy formally defined and documented (specifying CostCenter, Owner, Application, and Environment)?

options.label: Yes — formal policy covering required keys, allowed values, and inheritance rules
Standard documented but loosely adopted or inconsistent across teams
Informal conventions exist without formal documentation
No tagging strategy or metadata standard defined

questions.consultant_probe: Ask to see the written tagging standard. Check if there are case-sensitivity clashes (e.g. 'Environment' vs 'env') and whether shared services have defined allocation keys.
questions.subjective_prompt: Evaluate completeness of tagging standard and consistency across business units.
questions.remediation: Publish a mandatory tagging taxonomy (CostCenter, Owner, AppID, Env, DataClassification) with strict casing and value validation rules.

questions.text: What percentage of active compute and storage resources currently carry complete, valid mandatory tags in production and non-production?

options.label: ≥ 85% of total spend carries full, validated mandatory tags
60% – 84% tagged; key compute tagged but storage/network untagged
30% – 59% tagged with substantial unallocated spend
< 30% tagged; spend cannot be reliably mapped to teams

questions.consultant_probe: Run or ask for a cost allocation tag coverage report. Check untagged disks, snapshots and networking, which self-assessments often miss.
questions.subjective_prompt: Record actual tag coverage percentage, hardest resources to tag, and untagged spend dollar value.
questions.remediation: Establish a sprint goal to achieve ≥80% tag coverage on compute and storage, focusing on the top 20% of resources that generate 80% of spend.

questions.text: Is multi-cloud and hybrid cost data normalized using a common taxonomy or the FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification (FOCUS 1.0)?

options.label: Yes — normalized data model or FOCUS 1.0 specification adopted across all clouds
Single-cloud estate, or partial normalization across primary clouds
Multi-cloud data maintained in separate siloed spreadsheets/consoles
No normalization; impossible to compare cross-cloud usage

questions.consultant_probe: Ask how they compare AWS EC2 vs Azure VM vs GCP Compute Engine costs. Is there a normalized data model, or do analysts write bespoke SQL scripts for each provider?
questions.subjective_prompt: Note multi-cloud data pipeline tools (e.g. Snowflake, Databricks, CloudHealth, Apptio) and FOCUS adoption plans.
questions.remediation: Adopt the FOCUS specification (FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification, latest ratified version) to normalize multi-cloud billing into common columns such as BilledCost, EffectiveCost, ServiceName and ChargeCategory.

questions.text: Can engineering and product teams view their own team's cost data self-service without raising a ticket or waiting for monthly finance reports?

options.label: Yes — self-service dashboards filtered to team/application updated daily
Dashboards exist but require manual permission setup or are infrequently used
Teams can view top-level account cost but cannot filter to their workloads
Engineering teams have no visibility into their specific cost data

questions.consultant_probe: Ask an engineering lead to show where they look up yesterday's spend for their team. Is it on a live dashboard or completely hidden?
questions.subjective_prompt: Document developer access to cost dashboards, tool adoption rates, and feedback.
questions.remediation: Deploy role-based, team-filtered showback dashboards (e.g. QuickSight, PowerBI, Grafana, Cloudability) showing daily cost trends per product squad.

questions.text: How regularly are showback reports or automated spend summaries distributed to engineering leaders and business unit stakeholders?

options.label: Weekly or bi-weekly automated reports with trend analysis
Monthly showback reports distributed alongside finance reviews
Quarterly or ad-hoc reports only when leadership requests
No showback reporting exists

questions.consultant_probe: Check if showback is an automated proactive push (Slack/email digest) or a reactive report compiled only when budgets are blown.
questions.subjective_prompt: Capture showback frequency, recipients, and whether teams actively review reports.
questions.remediation: Automate a weekly showback digest highlighting top spend drivers, cost deltas, and month-to-date budget consumption for each engineering director.

questions.text: Is automated cost anomaly detection enabled and alerting on unexpected spend spikes within 24 hours of occurrence?

options.label: Yes — automated ML-based anomaly detection alerting within 24 hours to team channels
Cloud-native anomaly detection active on some accounts with email alerts
Static threshold alerts only; anomalies discovered during monthly bill review
No anomaly detection in place

questions.consultant_probe: Ask: 'If an engineer mistakenly deploys an unindexed vector DB cluster that burns $10k in a weekend, when does someone find out?'
questions.subjective_prompt: Record recent cost anomaly horror stories, threshold tuning, and response procedures.
questions.remediation: Turn on AWS Cost Anomaly Detection / Azure Cost Alerts with Slack/Teams webhooks configured to notify on-call engineers for spend spikes > $200/day.

questions.text: Are orphaned and idle resources (unattached EBS/disks, unassociated Elastic IPs, stale snapshots, idle load balancers) routinely identified?

options.label: Yes — continuous automated scans identify and flag orphaned resources weekly
Periodic manual audits conducted every few months
Identified opportunistically when cleaning up environments
Orphaned and idle resources are never scanned or tracked

questions.consultant_probe: Inspect their storage bill for snapshots and detached disks left behind by terminated instances, and ask who owns their clean-up.
questions.subjective_prompt: Estimate dollar value of idle resources and frequency of cleanup sprints.
questions.remediation: Schedule an immediate 'Cloud Janitor' cleanup sprint to delete unattached volumes, idle load balancers, and snapshots older than 90 days.

questions.text: How confidently can engineering teams explain their month-over-month cloud cost variances with specific business and architectural drivers?

options.label: Very confidently — variances tied directly to release changes, traffic volume, or unit scaling
Moderate confidence — explainable with research, but takes several days to diagnose
Low confidence — cost increases often unexplained or attributed to generic cloud growth
Teams have no awareness of their cost variances

questions.consultant_probe: Ask what caused last month's largest cost increase. If the answer is 'we don't know, maybe data transfer or traffic', accountability is weak.
questions.subjective_prompt: Gauge engineering familiarity with cost drivers (user growth vs inefficient code vs architectural leak).
questions.remediation: Incorporate a 15-minute monthly FinOps variance review into sprint retrospectives, requiring teams to account for changes >10% MoM.

questions.text: What formal cadence exists for reviewing cloud cost trends, forecasts, and optimization opportunities at team or BU level?

options.label: Monthly structured review with both engineering and finance leaders attending
Quarterly reviews tied to budget cycles
Ad-hoc reviews triggered only when budgets are overrun
No regular cost review cadence exists

questions.consultant_probe: Check if cost reviews are embedded into existing engineering sprint rituals or isolated into a dreaded annual procurement grilling.
questions.subjective_prompt: Document meeting cadence, attendance (finance vs engineering), and follow-through on action items.
questions.remediation: Establish a standing monthly Cloud Financial Review between Engineering Directors, Product Owners, and Finance Leads.

questions.text: What percentage of steady-state, eligible compute spend is covered by commitment-based discounts (Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, CUDs)?

options.label: ≥ 75% coverage with >95% commitment utilization managed centrally
50% – 74% coverage; some accounts optimized, others running purely on-demand
25% – 49% coverage; ad-hoc purchases without centralized tracking
< 25% coverage; vast majority running on expensive on-demand rates

questions.consultant_probe: Ask for their Compute Savings Plans and RI coverage and utilization percentages, and how they set the target coverage for steady-state workloads.
questions.subjective_prompt: Capture current commitment coverage %, utilization %, commitment expiration calendar, and purchasing policy.
questions.remediation: Centralize commitment purchasing at the management (payer) account and buy 1-year or 3-year Compute Savings Plans or reservations sized to the verified steady-state baseline.

questions.text: How regularly are instance rightsizing, CPU/memory downsizing, and modern generation upgrades (e.g. Graviton/ARM) reviewed and deployed?

options.label: Bi-weekly or monthly cadence with verified rightsizing actions deployed to production
Quarterly reviews; recommendations actioned for non-prod, slow for production
Rightsizing reviewed ad-hoc or only during infrastructure refresh
Instances are rarely or never rightsized after initial provisioning

questions.consultant_probe: Check if rightsizing recommendations in AWS Compute Optimizer or Azure Advisor sit in an untouched backlog or are actively converted into Jira tickets and deployed.
questions.subjective_prompt: Document rightsizing deployment blockers (e.g. fear of outages, lack of automated testing, dev team resistance).
questions.remediation: Dedicate 10% of engineering sprint capacity to deploy Compute Optimizer rightsizing recommendations, starting with non-prod and over-provisioned memory instances.

questions.text: Are Kubernetes / container cluster infrastructure costs broken down and allocated by namespace, deployment, pod, or microservice?

options.label: Yes — container cost allocation tool (e.g. Kubecost, OpenCost) active with pod-level showback
Cluster costs allocated using rough namespace node percentages or tag proxies
Cluster spend tracked as a single shared pool with no team breakdown
Containerized workloads have zero cost visibility

questions.consultant_probe: Ask how multi-tenant EKS/GKE/AKS cluster costs are distributed to product squads. Are clusters treated as a single massive black-box bill, or allocated via Kubecost/OpenCost?
questions.subjective_prompt: Detail container footprint (EKS/AKS/GKE/ECS), cluster tooling, and pod resource request vs limit discipline.
questions.remediation: Deploy OpenCost or Kubecost across your Kubernetes clusters to allocate node costs down to namespaces, controller workloads, and idle pod allocations.

questions.text: What share of eligible stateless, batch, CI/CD, or transient compute spend runs on Spot / Preemptible instances?

options.label: ≥ 50% of eligible stateless/batch workloads leverage Spot with automated eviction handling
20% – 49% Spot usage in dev/test or specific batch pipelines
< 20% Spot usage; perceived as too risky or complex
Zero Spot usage; everything runs on on-demand compute

questions.consultant_probe: Inspect CI/CD runners, batch processing, and non-prod Kubernetes worker nodes. Are they paying full on-demand pricing for disposable compute?
questions.subjective_prompt: Document Spot utilization, auto-scaler configuration (e.g. Karpenter), and interruption tolerance.
questions.remediation: Move fault-tolerant workloads such as CI/CD runners and dev Kubernetes node pools to Spot capacity, using an autoscaler such as Karpenter with interruption handling.

questions.text: Is cloud financial impact and unit cost a mandatory evaluation criterion in architectural reviews, RFCs, and major system design approvals?

options.label: Yes — estimated cost and unit economics are mandatory in all design reviews/RFCs
Cost is discussed informally but not formally modeled or audited
Cost is considered only for multi-million dollar projects
Architecture reviews evaluate performance and security only, ignoring cost

questions.consultant_probe: Review a recent Architecture Review Board (ARB) design document. Does it have an estimated monthly operating cost and unit economics section, or purely latency/HA diagrams?
questions.subjective_prompt: Assess whether cloud cost is designed in at inception or treated as an afterthought.
questions.remediation: Add a mandatory 'FinOps & Operating Cost Impact' section to your Architecture Review Board (ARB) templates before code is written.

questions.text: How are commitment-based discount portfolios (RIs, Savings Plans, CUDs) monitored for expiration, utilization drift, and break-even targets?

options.label: Continuous automated monitoring with staggered expiration pipeline and alerts
Tracked in a shared spreadsheet with quarterly renewal checks
Reactive renewals; commitments have expired unnoticed in the past
No tracking of commitment expirations or utilization

questions.consultant_probe: Ask who tracks expiring 1-year and 3-year commitments, and whether a commitment has ever expired unnoticed and caused an on-demand spend spike.
questions.subjective_prompt: Review commitment renewal calendar and portfolio hedging strategy.
questions.remediation: Implement a rolling commitment strategy with staggered expirations every quarter to smooth budget impact and prevent cliff-edge renewals.

questions.text: Has data transfer, cross-AZ traffic, NAT Gateway data processing, and public egress been reviewed and optimized with architectural controls?

options.label: Yes — VPC endpoints, direct interconnects, and local AZ routing active; egress audited quarterly
VPC endpoints deployed for top services (S3/Dynamo), but cross-AZ traffic unoptimized
Egress acknowledged as high but no architectural remediation implemented
Data transfer and cross-AZ traffic are unmonitored and unoptimized

questions.consultant_probe: Look at the NAT Gateway, cross-AZ and inter-region data transfer line items, and ask whether anyone owns network cost for microservices traffic.
questions.subjective_prompt: Document network topology, VPC endpoints, CloudFront caching, and cross-AZ traffic patterns.
questions.remediation: Deploy VPC Gateway Endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB and configure zonal DNS routing to eliminate expensive NAT Gateway and cross-AZ transfer charges.

questions.text: To what extent are engineering teams recognized, celebrated, or rewarded for eliminating cloud waste and improving architectural efficiency?

options.label: Active recognition — FinOps achievements celebrated in all-hands, bonuses, or hackathons
Informal shout-outs in team retrospectives for major savings
Cost savings expected but never publicly recognized or rewarded
Feature velocity is rewarded exclusively; cost optimization is invisible

questions.consultant_probe: Ask engineers: 'Do you get recognition in performance reviews or all-hands for saving $50k/month in cloud waste, or only for shipping features?'
questions.subjective_prompt: Evaluate organizational incentives, gamification leaderboards, and engineering leadership support.
questions.remediation: Launch an internal 'FinOps Champions' recognition award and highlight top waste-reduction stories in engineering monthly town halls.

questions.text: Does a dedicated cost optimization backlog exist and get groomed alongside functional features in regular engineering sprints?

options.label: Yes — dedicated FinOps epics/stories with quantified ROI groomed in standard sprints
Stories created occasionally but routinely deprioritized for functional features
Ad-hoc tickets created only when finance rings alarm bells
No cost optimization stories exist in engineering backlogs

questions.consultant_probe: Check their Jira / Azure DevOps backlog. Are FinOps tickets tagged with estimated monthly savings and prioritized by ROI?
questions.subjective_prompt: Review Jira backlog for FinOps stories, prioritization criteria, and completion velocity.
questions.remediation: Tag optimization tickets in Jira with estimated monthly savings (e.g. '$2,400/mo savings · 4 story points') to enable data-driven sprint prioritization.

questions.text: Rank these optimization levers by historical ROI in your estate: Commitments, Rightsizing, Storage Lifecycle, and Spot/Autoscaling.

options.label: All four levers actively harvested across steady-state workloads
Commitments and storage lifecycle mature; rightsizing and spot nascent
Commitments only; usage optimization and rightsizing not executed
None of these optimization levers have been systematically deployed

questions.consultant_probe: Evaluate which levers have matured vs which are completely neglected by their infrastructure teams.
questions.subjective_prompt: Document realized savings across each lever over the past 12 months.
questions.remediation: Balance rate optimization (quick financial wins) with architectural usage optimization (permanent engineering efficiency) for compounded ROI.

questions.text: Is tagging and cost governance enforced automatically through policy-as-code guardrails (e.g. OPA, Terraform Sentinel, Azure Policy, SCPs)?

options.label: Yes — automated policy gates block non-compliant deployments in CI/CD and at cloud API level
Policies configured in audit mode (flags violations but does not block)
Linting rules exist in some repos but no central enforcement gate
No policy-as-code or automated guardrails exist

questions.consultant_probe: Test whether an engineer can deploy an untagged EC2 instance or Azure VM via CLI/Terraform right now. Does the CI/CD pipeline or cloud policy immediately block or quarantine it?
questions.subjective_prompt: Assess policy-as-code enforcement tools, bypass mechanisms, and automated remediation bots.
questions.remediation: Convert tagging and instance-family guidelines into strict policy-as-code guardrails in Terraform/OpenTofu and Azure Policy / AWS SCPs to block non-compliant deployments.

questions.text: Are non-production resources (dev, test, staging environments) automatically parked or shut down outside working hours and on weekends?

options.label: Yes — default automated schedule stops non-prod outside 8am-6pm weekdays with easy opt-out
Automated schedules active for some teams; others run 24/7 continuously
Engineers are asked to stop instances manually (infrequently done)
All non-production environments run 24/7 by default

questions.consultant_probe: Check whether non-prod compute runs 24/7 (about 730 hours a month) or on a business-hours schedule, and whether parking is automated.
questions.subjective_prompt: Document auto-parking tools (AWS Instance Scheduler, Cloud Custodian, Azure Automation) and opt-out rate.
questions.remediation: Deploy automated environment schedulers across all dev and staging accounts to power down compute outside core business hours.

questions.text: Do automated lifecycle policies govern object storage tiering (e.g. S3 Intelligent-Tiering / Glacier, Azure Blob cool/archive) and snapshot TTL expiration?

options.label: Yes — comprehensive lifecycle rules automatically transition and expire storage across all buckets
Lifecycle rules active on primary buckets; secondary storage unmanaged
Manual cleanup scripts run occasionally when storage bills escalate
No automated lifecycle policies exist; data accumulates indefinitely

questions.consultant_probe: Check S3/Blob storage classes. Are petabytes of log data or backups sitting on S3 Standard / Blob Hot storage that hasn't been accessed in 180 days?
questions.subjective_prompt: Audit object storage lifecycle policies, snapshot retention scripts, and archive usage.
questions.remediation: Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering across all production buckets and enforce a 30-day lifecycle rule on debug logs and ephemeral test snapshots.

questions.text: Are modern AI / GenAI and GPU infrastructure costs tracked with idle model endpoint shutdown, GPU utilization metrics, and token cost attribution?

options.label: Yes — dedicated GenAI FinOps tracking GPU cluster saturation, token attribution, and idle shutdown
LLM API spend tracked at account level, but GPU utilization and prompt caching unmonitored
AI spend lumped into general cloud compute with zero visibility into model economics
No AI workloads in cloud, or AI spend completely unmanaged

questions.consultant_probe: Ask how they track spending on OpenAI/Anthropic APIs, AWS Bedrock, SageMaker, or Azure OpenAI. Are dedicated GPU clusters sitting idle over weekends at $10k/day?
questions.subjective_prompt: Document GenAI architecture, dedicated GPU cluster count, prompt token tracking, and caching mechanisms.
questions.remediation: Implement automatic scale-to-zero on SageMaker/Azure ML inference endpoints and enforce semantic prompt caching to cut recurring model inference costs.

questions.text: Are container resource requests and limits (CPU/Memory) tuned automatically using Horizontal/Vertical Pod Autoscalers (HPA/VPA) or Karpenter?

options.label: Yes — automated VPA/HPA tuning with intelligent node bin-packing (e.g. Karpenter)
HPA configured based on traffic; pod requests tuned manually every few months
Static pod requests set high to prevent OOM errors, causing massive cluster slack
No pod requests/limits configured; nodes run in unbalanced, unoptimized states

questions.consultant_probe: Compare Kubernetes pod resource requests with actual CPU and memory utilization, and ask how requests are set and reviewed.
questions.subjective_prompt: Evaluate VPA/Karpenter adoption, namespace quota enforcement, and node pool bin-packing efficiency.
questions.remediation: Deploy Vertical Pod Autoscaler in recommendation mode to rightsize container CPU/Memory requests, eliminating massive cluster slack.

questions.text: Are FinOps efficiency metrics formally included in engineering team OKRs, sprint KPIs, or performance evaluations?

options.label: Yes — explicit cost-efficiency OKRs (e.g. unit cost reduction, zero untagged compute) in sprint KPIs
Discussed at director level, but not cascaded into individual engineering squad OKRs
Mentioned informally when budgets are tight, but not part of performance reviews
Cost efficiency plays zero role in engineering OKRs or evaluations

questions.consultant_probe: Ask the VP of Engineering: 'Are your engineering managers held accountable for unit efficiency and cost targets in their quarterly performance reviews?'
questions.subjective_prompt: Document existing engineering OKRs and how cost efficiency is weighted against delivery velocity.
questions.remediation: Incorporate a standardized FinOps Key Result into engineering squad quarterly OKRs (e.g. 'Maintain <5% unallocated spend and rightsizing compliance ≥90%').

questions.text: Does automated handling, graceful draining, and instant replacement exist for Spot / Preemptible instance interruptions?

options.label: Yes — automated node drainer and diversified capacity pools ensure zero-downtime Spot resilience
Basic autoscaler handles replacements, but transient failures can occur
Spot used only for batch tasks that can afford hard crashes
No automated interruption handling; Spot cannot be used for application services

questions.consultant_probe: Verify if Spot termination notices (AWS 2-minute warning) trigger automated node draining and replacement via Karpenter/Cluster Autoscaler without dropping user traffic.
questions.subjective_prompt: Review Spot resilience architecture and zero-downtime test results.
questions.remediation: Implement AWS Node Termination Handler or Karpenter capacity rebalancing to drain and rotate Spot instances before cloud termination.

questions.text: Over the last rolling quarter, what has been your cloud spend forecast variance against actual monthly billing?

options.label: Within ± 5% variance consistently across quarters
Within ± 15% variance; major product launches sometimes cause drift
Within ± 30% variance; forecasts are rough approximations
> 30% variance or no formal cloud spend forecast is produced

questions.consultant_probe: Ask Finance and Cloud Ops to compare their forecasted spend from 90 days ago against the actual invoiced total. Is variance within 5% or 40% off?
questions.subjective_prompt: Record actual forecast variance percentage, forecasting tools, and driver-based modeling capabilities.
questions.remediation: Build a driver-based rolling forecast model combining historical run-rate trends with product roadmap launch schedules to maintain variance within ±5%.

questions.text: Do software and DevOps engineers receive automated cost feedback inside their normal workflow (e.g. Infracost in GitHub/GitLab pull requests)?

options.label: Yes — automated PR comments show exact estimated dollar impact before code is merged
PR cost checks deployed on some core repositories but not universal
Cost discussed manually during code reviews for high-risk changes
Engineers merge infrastructure code with zero automated cost visibility

questions.consultant_probe: Ask to see a sample Pull Request. Does Infracost comment directly on the PR showing: 'This Terraform change will increase monthly AWS spend by $340'?
questions.subjective_prompt: Assess shift-left FinOps tooling (Infracost, Terraform cost estimators) and developer response.
questions.remediation: Integrate Infracost into GitHub/GitLab CI/CD pipelines to show engineers the real-time cost delta of Terraform/CloudFormation PRs before merging.

questions.text: How mature is financial chargeback to business units, product lines, and cost centers (actual financial transfer to P&Ls)?

options.label: Fully automated chargeback with monthly journal entries posted to SAP/Oracle general ledgers
Showback is enforced with budget accountability, but no direct P&L debit
Informal chargeback based on rough percentage splits with frequent disputes
Centralized IT absorbs all cloud costs as corporate overhead with zero chargeback

questions.consultant_probe: Verify whether chargeback is actual journal entries debiting BU general ledgers or just 'showback' reports that directors can ignore with zero budget consequence.
questions.subjective_prompt: Document financial ledger integration, dispute resolution processes, and shared platform allocation keys.
questions.remediation: Transition from informational showback to direct automated chargeback in your ERP (SAP/Oracle/NetSuite), holding business unit leaders financially accountable for their cloud consumption.

questions.text: Are business unit economics defined, tracked, and reported in real-time (e.g. cost per transaction, cost per active user, cost per order)?

options.label: Yes — granular unit metrics (cost/transaction, cost/tenant) tracked and trended on executive dashboards
Unit metrics calculated manually on a quarterly basis for key products
Top-level cloud spend tracked against revenue, but no operational unit metrics
No unit economics defined; cloud spend treated solely as a lump-sum IT expense

questions.consultant_probe: Ask the client's executive: 'What is your cloud infrastructure cost per completed customer order or active subscriber, and has it increased or decreased over the last 12 months?'
questions.subjective_prompt: Document defined unit economics metrics, data source integrations, and executive reporting frequency.
questions.remediation: Define 1-2 core unit economic metrics (e.g. Cloud Cost per 1,000 Transactions) combining cloud billing telemetry with product analytics in BI dashboards.

questions.text: Is cloud cost and unit telemetry integrated directly into enterprise BI platforms and long-range corporate financial planning?

options.label: Yes — cloud unit telemetry feeds directly into corporate BI and FP&A financial models
Cloud costs integrated into BI dashboards, but FP&A models use manual quarterly inputs
Separate reporting tracks; cloud team tools do not communicate with finance BI
Cloud financials completely isolated from corporate BI platforms

questions.consultant_probe: Check if CFO forecasting models incorporate real-time cloud unit cost metrics, or if cloud budgets are forecasted as a flat 15% annual increase.
questions.subjective_prompt: Evaluate FP&A involvement in cloud budgeting and multi-year forecasting accuracy.
questions.remediation: Feed normalized cloud cost data directly into the enterprise data warehouse (Snowflake/BigQuery) so FP&A can model cloud COGS against product revenue pipelines.

questions.text: Is infrastructure cost per customer or tenant tracked and used directly to inform product tier pricing, enterprise contracts, and margin defense?

options.label: Yes — exact cost-to-serve per customer is tracked and informs contract pricing and tier margins
Calculated for high-tier enterprise clients during annual contract renewals
Rough approximations used; individual customer cloud cost unknown
No tracking of customer cost-to-serve; all customers billed standard pricing

questions.consultant_probe: Ask Sales / Product: 'Do you know which of your enterprise customers are unprofitable due to heavy cloud compute/storage consumption?'
questions.subjective_prompt: Detail multi-tenant cost tracking capabilities and how it informs bespoke enterprise contract pricing.
questions.remediation: Implement customer-tenant attribution tags on storage and compute to identify unprofitable enterprise accounts and adjust renewal pricing.

questions.text: How embedded are executive FinOps scorecards, department leaderboards, and peer benchmarking in driving executive behavior?

options.label: Highly embedded — monthly executive scorecards drive competition and senior accountability
Scorecards shared with department heads quarterly; discussed at leadership reviews
Scorecards distributed informally without executive sponsorship
No scorecards or peer benchmarks exist

questions.consultant_probe: Check if business unit leaders compare their unit costs against other internal BUs on monthly executive scorecards.
questions.subjective_prompt: Review executive scorecard metrics and C-suite engagement.
questions.remediation: Publish an executive 'Cloud Efficiency Scorecard' ranking business units by tag compliance, commitment coverage, and unit cost trajectory.

questions.text: What proportion of the total cloud bill is currently attributable to unallocated waste, idle compute, or unattached storage?

options.label: < 4% of total spend — lean, autonomous estate with continuous self-healing guardrails
4% – 9% waste — healthy posture with minor occasional drift
10% – 20% waste — regular cleanups required to keep spend in check
> 20% waste — significant ongoing waste across multiple accounts

questions.consultant_probe: Verify the client's estimate against their idle and unallocated spend reports, and ask how the estimate was produced.
questions.subjective_prompt: Analyze client's waste percentage and ongoing posture defense mechanisms.
questions.remediation: Implement automated guardrails (for example, quarantine unattached disks after 7 days) and track idle and unallocated spend as a KPI with an agreed target.

questions.text: To what extent does cloud cost efficiency, unit economics, and margin optimization feature in senior leadership performance evaluations and compensation?

options.label: Formally tied to executive KPIs, bonus incentives, and performance reviews
Considered during annual performance reviews as part of overall operational rigor
Evaluated only if massive budget overruns occur
Plays zero role in leadership evaluations or compensation

questions.consultant_probe: Ask if engineering directors and VP-level leaders have performance bonuses tied to cloud gross margin targets.
questions.subjective_prompt: Assess leadership compensation structures and incentives.
questions.remediation: Align leadership incentives by tying a portion of engineering executive bonuses to achieving gross margin and unit cost efficiency targets.

questions.text: Do cloud unit economics and margin data directly inform product feature deprecation, architecture rewrites, and expansion decisions?

options.label: Yes — product roadmaps and feature lifecycle decisions are routinely steered by unit margin data
Considered during major product overhauls, but not continuously during feature planning
Informally acknowledged, but feature velocity always trumps margin data
Product teams never consult cloud cost data when planning roadmaps

questions.consultant_probe: Ask: 'Have you ever killed an unprofitable feature or rewritten an architecture because its cloud unit cost eroded customer margin?'
questions.subjective_prompt: Capture specific examples of product strategy influenced by cloud unit economics.
questions.remediation: Embed FinOps architects into the product roadmap lifecycle to audit the unit economics of new features prior to general availability.

archetypes.name: Cloud-Native B2B SaaS Scale-up
archetypes.description: Fast-growing high-velocity SaaS. Heavy EKS cluster footprint. Engineers spin up resources freely. Good awareness but tagging is inconsistent and 40% of compute runs on expensive on-demand instances.

archetypes.name: Tier-1 Enterprise Bank & Capital Markets
archetypes.description: Heavily regulated global financial institution. Strong account boundaries and centralized procurement. However, rightsizing approvals take months, container allocation is unmapped, and on-demand legacy spend leaks millions.

archetypes.name: Healthcare & Life Sciences Network
archetypes.description: Research hospital and diagnostics platform. Enormous petabyte-scale genomics and imaging datasets. Dedicated GPU clusters for AI model training frequently sit idle, driving up cloud bills with minimal unit attribution.

archetypes.name: Global Retail & Omnichannel E-Commerce
archetypes.description: High seasonal transaction volume with huge Black Friday/holiday elasticity. Significant cross-AZ data transfer costs and NAT Gateway processing fees. Good automated scheduling in dev, but lacks real-time unit economics per order.
